items.note: S1.3.1.1 gives the three-stage exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) on three-element subsets, with scratch restored, but calls all three stages forward invocations, whereas stage 2 is the inverse schedule from Y to X (731-733, 761-763). It also omits h=100, N, m and the cancellation (JV+RG)x=x. No derivation is shown.

It states that a common frame commutes with pointwise linear gates and that only the endpoint operator acts. It drops the routing rho and the sign epsilon_w of eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} (818-822), and it does not write D_out S D_in^{-1}.

The plan states that the labels are nested and nondegenerate and that only central-wire edges decrease, and it gives L<N/2 in words. It omits the triple-indicator construction, the loss h from time 3 to 4, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539.

The plan states s<Wm and says that the endpoint matrices give H<-H+D on every role. It never states the projection assignment (P_U, with -P_{U_a} at the source), the identity M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m, or s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

Correct as far as it goes: one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s calls in all, and C-tensor on every role after the corrections. It omits the definition of C_U through i^{wt(P_U x)}, the formula s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, and the weight-additivity proof.

It gives s<Wm because L<N/2, s/W<m^tau and tau=1-2^{-50}. The deficits eta_b and eta_c are missing, as is the argument eta>20*2^{-50} with log m<20 that justifies tau, so tau=1-2^{-50} appears only as a parameter choice.
S1.1 matches Lemma lem:elementary-streams. S1.2 omits the prime radix q, the modulus q^b and the requirement that the offset be computable in b^{O(1)} time.

The route matches the paper: factor E_1 Pi E_2, apply the triangular factors by controlled shifts, then one interchange per one of Pi. Two steps are missing: the elimination proof of the factorization (1375-1392) and the choice of a fixed odd prime q that avoids the denominators (1413-1423).

The paper's route: a cyclic role-stream split, edge shears done by recursive interchanges, H<-H+D, the three-update interchange, s calls of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and F_k=O(e^tau). The statement says only 'enough rows' where the paper requires a row count divisible by W^k. The fixed-tape O(V) schedule is not spelled out.

The base-m pieces, padding rows to a multiple of W^k, and binary-to-radix-q padding are all there. The essential step of taking rho=O(log e) high digits of the chunks as the row field (1650-1681) is missing, so the plan never says where the rows come from.

It has the kernel product, exactly s child calls on e/m axes, no extra calls from the corrections, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. Three things are missing: the conjugation by P_M that puts the residual directions into coordinate slots, its realization by row additions, and the identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z.

This follows the paper: eight conditional rotations that restore w, packed cyclic shifts that are correct away from a guard set of fraction 80(f-1)2^{-K}, repair by extraction and radix sort, and O(V(L^tau+1)) in the parameter family. The permutation argument for T_0 S_0^{-1} on B is left implicit.

The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) is stated correctly, with its reason. Missing are the rows drawn from the first q_0 chunks, the leaf bound e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}, K<=e^{c/beta}, and the condition max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda'.

It has the O(Vd^{lambda'}) cost, the error below sqrt2 2^{-p} and one truncation, and the guard-bit route (depth bound 8B^2 d^{nu+1}, the grid and modulus induction, Delta=o(p) from epsilon C_1<1), all as in the paper.

The cost dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}, character cancellation, decimation in frequency and bit-reversed order are all correct. Missing are the layout permutation L in the counterpart LBF^-, the error bound sqrt2 l 2^{-p}, and the argument that J_E commutes with Q_p, which gives one truncation per round.
Evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, |h_j|<B_0/2, centered extraction with a 0/1 carry, the negacyclic reduction, the shift by p+l, and four products costing O(rp log(rp)): all as in the paper.

The retained LB order, pointwise products, the opposite transform, the scale M=T/r, the error M(3delta+eta), and the disk condition all match. The normalization identity is cited only through the motivation.

The identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, the Neumann-series route, the error and time bounds, and the tensor form with axis exposure all match. The definitions of P_s and P_t and the hypothesis theta>p/alpha^4 are not stated at this step.
Both identities are stated correctly, and S5.4 gives the right reason for cancellation. The chirp a is never defined and its coefficient check is absent. Getting RF^+ by conjugation is not stated.
The exponents, sizes, prime intervals, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta>p and no wraparound all follow the paper. The list omits lambda=1-2^{-52} and the explicit eta=1/(4d) and alpha.
The isomorphism x->prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular coordinates done as prefix-controlled shifts in the order i=d..1, and the cost O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)), as in the paper.
The twist by zeta^k, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g), all as in the paper. The computed twist errors are not mentioned.
The source-transform composition with exact counterpart RF_s and the six steps of the algorithm match the paper. The definition of F^+ by conjugation is not stated.

The contraction error calculus, E_s, the product error, E_w, the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding and carries all follow the paper. The intermediate ring and chirp errors (5TL, 8TL) are skipped.
The margins g_1..g_7, min=2^{-181}=2kappa, the row-by-row justification, the o(Tp) setup and the final O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) match. S7.7 quotes the bad fraction slightly loosely.
It states that the limit is zero along all lengths, so no constant c_A gives an eventual lower bound. This matches the paper's introduction, which offers no further derivation.

errors.says: Three stages of forward invocations send (X_a,Y_a) to (-Y_a,X_a).
errors.paper: Stage 1 is a forward invocation from X to Y, stage 2 is the inverse forward schedule from Y to X (effecting X<-X-Y), and stage 3 is forward again.

errors.says: Only the endpoint operator D_sink D_source^{-1} acts on each role.
errors.paper: Route w->rho(w) applies eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, so the role is permuted and a scalar sign is applied.

errors.says: Each edge's orthogonal residual has dimension equal to the number of smaller operations the edge needs.
errors.paper: This holds for every edge except the N source edges on X_a in the bit network, whose edge matrix 2P_{U_a} has rank one while the dimension change is zero.
The bad-address fraction is O(d 2^{-K}) (80(f-1)2^{-K} in the lemma).

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from start to finish: chunk interchange, then the simultaneous layer, synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling and chirp, the multiplication algorithm, exact recovery, and the cost table that gives O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). It thins out at the central saving. S1.3.1.4 asserts s<Wm because L<N/2, but the budget sum|Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L is missing, as are rank equals dimension change, the endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m, and the derivation of tau=1-2^{-50} from the deficits. The rows taken from high digits in S1.4 and the row construction of the layer recurrence are also missing.

steps.note: It has a fixed network on three-element subsets, the exchange (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), and every scratch wire restored. h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are not stated (m appears only as the label dimension), so this is a borderline verdict.
A common frame per gate commutes with pointwise linear gates, the intermediate frames cancel, and only the endpoint operator acts. The routing and sign are omitted.
It states nested nondegenerate labels in an m-dimensional bilinear space with only central-wire edges decreasing. It does not say F^{tensor 3}, the times 3->4 or the loss h, so this is borderline.

The plan equates residual dimension with the number of operations and alludes to 'source ranks the rational interface adds'. It never states that rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U or that the N source edges have rank one.
The budget sum|Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b are all absent. The plan only speaks of summing residual dimensions.
It states the condition L<N/2 (in words: less than half the N added source ranks) and concludes s<Wm. The exact ratios 100/539 and 101/539 are missing.
It says the endpoint matrices give H<-H+D on every role, scratch roles included. It does not state M_sink(rho(w))-M_source(w)=I_m or the projection assignment that produces it.
It has the E_1 Pi E_2 factorization, exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and s recursive calls in all, the sum of the edge ranks.
It has role streams of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau, F_k=O(e^tau) and tau=1-2^{-50}. The justification of tau from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 is absent.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the frame (C1-C3) and recursion (C8-C9) ends of the central saving and asserts the strict saving L<N/2 => s<Wm. Three links that make the saving quantitative are only alluded to: rank equals dimension change, with rank-one source exceptions (C4); the budget Wm-2N+2L, which turns into s_b=Wm-N+2L (C5); and the endpoint identity M_sink-M_source=I_m (C7). Six of the nine steps are reconstructed, several of them borderline.
